playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- “나는 F1 게임을 만들고 싶어” — build a complete, playable Formula racing game with manual gears, RPM, grip loss, and a high-quality racing-game presentation; a race mode is sufficient.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game now without asking clarifying questions.
- Aim for F1 2011-like simulation depth and polished visuals; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Implemented a self-contained browser game using Canvas and custom JavaScript physics/rendering, with a Monza-inspired 3-lap race, rather than external game-engine dependencies.
- Used keyboard and mobile touch controls; manual shifting uses Q/E.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js` implementing the racing game, HUD, race start, pause/help, opponents, tyre grip/wear, RPM, throttle/brake, ERS, and sound toggle.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Browser opened at `http://localhost:3002`; no JavaScript console errors were observed (only missing `/favicon.ico` 404).
- Captured and read `screenshots/apex.jpg`.

### Active
- Review visual/gameplay quality and fix any issues identified.
- Consider adding a favicon or suppressing its 404 if appropriate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/apex.jpg` if visual refinement is needed and test starting/driving/shifting/pause in the browser.
2. Fix any discovered rendering or gameplay issues.
3. Summarize implementation and controls for the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game DOM and HUD structure.
- `style.css`: Full-screen responsive styling and start panel.
- `game.js`: Canvas renderer, race simulation, physics, controls, HUD.
- `screenshots/apex.jpg`: Latest browser screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Controls: W/↑ accelerate, S/↓ brake, A/D steer, Q/E manual down/upshift, Space ERS boost, P pause, Enter or “RACE START” to begin.

content.text:
Let me continue: test the game by driving it via CDP. I have chromium running with remote debugging on 9222. Let me check if it's up, and use a script to connect via WebSocket. Is there a ws library? Let me check.

Actually, I need to evaluate gameplay quality. The game is decent but several things need improvement to hit "F1 2011 level":

Key issues visible/known:
1. No rev limiter / gear ratio driven speed properly (speed capped artificially at 93 m/s = 335 km/h; engine RPM computed from wheel speed but shifting has no real consequence — if you stay in 1st gear you can reach top speed? Actually RPM clamps at 13700 and torque stays; speed isn't limited by gear. That's a physics flaw: no gear-dependent top speed. Should make acceleration force depend on RPM/torque properly and limit by gear ratio; if in gear 1 you should hit rev limiter at ~90 km/h.
2. Steering: `car.lateral` uses progress and steering; track curve visually shifts and the car must steer to follow. But curveAt is not connected to the car's lateral position — there's no actual requirement to steer through corners; corners are only visual bends. This is a big gameplay issue: you can drive straight through Eau Rouge-like bends without steering. F1 2011 quality needs cornering to matter.

Let me improve the model: compute track curvature at car progress, and require the car to steer; lateral drift due to cornering (centrifugal force pushing outward). Add off-track detection with grass slowdown. Add rivals you can overtake (positions computed by progress okay).

But careful: changing physics significantly could break playability without testing. Let me at least implement:
- Gear-limited top speed via engine force → speed integration using torque curve and drag; add rev limiter: RPM max 13700 cuts torque.
- Add curvature-based centrifugal lateral force so player must steer.

Also the visuals: currently it looks like an arcade POV racer with flat green ground, decent. To be "high quality", add:
- Better ground (grass texture stripes), tyre marks, gravel traps, more detailed barriers, grandstands with crowds, bridge, marshal posts.
- Car shadow already.
- Add motion blur? Keep simple.

Also lap timing: best/last lap, sector times? F1 2011-like HUD includes lap delta. Could add last lap time display.

Also race finish: results panel needed. Finish currently just pauses with message; no results. Add a results card with final position, time, laps. Also restart button. Important for "complete game".

Also the start: formation lap label but no countdown lights. Add F1-style 5 red lights start sequence with rolling start hold. That's a big quality factor. Implement pre-start lights sequence after clicking RACE START: 5 lights each 0.9s then lights out; player must hold throttle; jump start ignored.

Also opponents should be visible ahead at race start (they start ahead). Fine.

Also position starts P08 and 7 opponents — good.

Sound: engine sound placeholder; add tyre/kerb sounds maybe fine.

Let me be strategic: implement meaningful upgrades:

1. Start light sequence (F1 2011-style).
2. Realistic gearing: top speed per gear via RPM limiter; auto clutch? Manual only with Q/E, but if player doesn't shift, limiter bounces. Add auto-upshift? No — manual requested. But add a "shift indicator" flash when RPM near limiter.
3. Corner physics: lateral G from curvature, must steer to hold line; off track and corner cut penalties.
4. Lap timing with best lap + sector delta in HUD.
5. Results screen + restart.
6. Visual polish: grandstands, crowds, gravel traps, sponsor boards, skyline, start gantry lights, skid marks? Keep performance okay.

Let me first test the current game via CDP to see behavior and capture mid-race screenshot. Check for a websocket client; Node 22 has built-in WebSocket. Let me write a CDP script.

Let me check node version and the debugging endpoint.

Then design the physics carefully.

Physics design (units m/s):
- Gear ratios: [0, 3.15, 2.45, 1.94, 1.60, 1.36, 1.18, 1.04, .94] (final drive implicit). Wheel radius 0.33 m. RPM = speed / (2π r) * ratio * finalDrive * 60. Current formula: speed/.33*ratio*3.25*60/(2π) — that's speed/(2π*0.33)*ratio*3.25*60 = speed*ratio*3.25*60/(2.073) ≈ speed*ratio*94.1. At 93 m/s in 8th: 93*0.94*94.1 ≈ 8226 rpm. Hmm that's low vs 13700. So top speed isn't limited by RPM. Let's calibrate: want 8th gear at ~340 km/h (94.4 m/s) ≈ 12000 rpm. So factor k such that rpm = speed * ratio * k → 94.4*0.94*k = 12000 → k = 135.2. Then gear 1 at 12000 rpm: speed = 12000/(3.15*135.2) = 28.2 m/s = 101 km/h. Reasonable.

So rpm = speed * ratio * 135.2 + idle-ish. At standstill 4200 idle. Use rpm = max(idle, speed*ratio*135).

Torque curve: peak ~ around 10500-11500 rpm. torqueFactor = 1 - 0.4*((rpm-11000)/6500)^2 maybe. Force = enginePower... Simplify: accel = torqueFactor * maxAccel * (throttle) / (1 + speed*0.02) with gear? Real accel in low gear higher due to torque multiplication. Could do wheelForce = torque * ratio, but then top speed limited by drag. Simpler: compute engine force F = torqueFactor * 9000 * ratio/3.15? That would make 1st gear enormous. Use wheel force proportional to ratio/final: F = torqueFactor * ratio * 2500 N. Mass 800 kg → accel = F/800. In 1st: 1*3.15*2500/800 = 9.8 m/s² nice. In 8th: 0.94*2500/800 = 2.9 m/s². Drag = 0.5*rho*CdA*v² ≈ 0.0045*v²? Current aero = .0045 * v² (force per mass?) at 93 → 39 N/kg?? That's huge. They used aero as force divided by 820 mass: aero=.0045*v² and dividing by 820 → at 93: 38.9/820 = 0.047 m/s². Too small. Hmm whatever.

Let's define:
- mass 798 kg
- drag force = 0.55 * v² (CdA*rho/2 ≈ 0.5*1.225*1.5*0.9? Actually F1 CdA ≈ 1.5 m², so 0.5*1.225*1.5 = 0.92; use 0.9 v²) → at 94 m/s = 7950 N; power needed = 747 kW ≈ 1000 hp, high but F1 ~ 750 kW total with ERS. Fine.
- rolling resistance = 0.015 * mass * g = 117 N.
- engine force at wheel: torque at wheel / r. Let's target accel: 0-100 km/h in ~2.6 s. Use gear 1 force ~ 11000 N → accel 13.8 m/s². So torque factor*ratio*K = 11000 at ratio 3.15 → K = 3492. Let's set engineForce = torqueFactor * 3600 * ratio * throttle * ersFactor. At ratio 3.15 and torqueFactor ~0.9 → 10200 N → accel 12.8. Good.
- In 8th at 12000 rpm torqueFactor ~1 → F = 3384 N, drag at 94 = 7950 → can't reach. Hmm top speed would then be lower. Balance: reduce drag coefficient to 0.42 v² → at 94: 3710 N vs 3384 → top ~90 m/s (324 km/h). Fine for Monza with DRS. Let's use 0.38 v² and torqueFactor*ratio*3600: top ~ 95 m/s in 8th at 12000 rpm. Good.

RPM limiter: when rpm >= 13400, engine force cuts (bounce). Player must upshift. Downshift protection: if downshifting would exceed limiter (rpm after shift > 13000), reject with "DOWNSHIFT BLOCKED". Auto-blip? Keep simple.

Also clutch on start: if gear 1 and throttle, rpm rises. We can fake standstill launch: if speed < 1 → rpm = 4200 + throttle*8000; engine force uses launch torque; that's fine.

Anti-stall if in too high gear at low speed: rpm low → torqueFactor reduced; add "turbo lag"? For playability, if rpm < 5000 engine force weak; so starting in 2nd is slow. Good.

Steering / curvature:
- Track curvature at car progress: derive from curveAt? The visual dx is accumulated. Define a curvature function c(p) = curveAt(p) scaled. Let's define lateral curvature in "lateral units per second": the track's center at the car's position shifts as you progress. In the renderer, bend at distance d ≈ dx * t where dx accumulates curve. That corresponds to world lateral offset per distance of ~ curveAt * d * 0.08... Let's simplify: define track curvature K(p) in 1/m via smooth function; the required player lateral velocity to stay centered is -? Hmm.

Simpler gameplay: derive "corner force" from curveAt: curveAt returns ~±0.0015 near corners. Multiply by something to get lateral drift. Use `bend = curveAt(car.progress) * 8000` giving ~±12; then centrifugal = bend * speed * 0.01 → lateral drift velocity. Let's think: we want a strong corner (e.g., Parabolica) to push the car outward at speed, requiring steering input.

Current lateral model: lateral += (steerResponse - lateral*damp)*dt, steerResponse = steer*speedFactor*0.36*grip*(1-slip*.56); speedFactor = speed/22 capped 1.5 → at 90 m/s = 1.5, so response 0.54 per second max steering; damp = min(speed*0.006,0.4) = 0.4. So steady lateral ≈ 0.3/0.4... plus. It works as an arcade lateral position within ±1.45. Track edges at |lateral|>0.88 off track.

Add centrifugal: corner = curveAt(progress)*something → lateral -= corner*speed? curvature sign: right-hand positive? curveAt sign indicates curve direction; if positive, track bends right (x offset increases). The car should be pushed left (outward) relative to track, i.e., lateral decreases. Let's add lateralVelocity: define car.latVel instead of direct response? Better dynamic: car.latVel += (steerInput * steerPower - latVel*damp + centrifugal)*dt; car.lateral += latVel*dt. Let's define:
- steerPower = 2.4 * clamp(speed/30,0,1.6) (lateral units/s²?) Hmm need scaling in units of track-half-width per second.

Simpler and robust: keep existing model but add drift term: lateralResponse includes -curve*speed*constant.

Let's compute realistic centrifugal lateral acceleration = v² * K where K = 1/R. Steering lateral accel = v²/R_max. In lateral units where 1 unit = half track width (~6 m), steering at 90 m/s should be able to produce maybe 0.8 units/s lateral velocity. Time to cross track ~1.2 s. That's plausible.

Rather than physical accuracy, tune for feel: 
centrifugal = -curveSign * speedFactor * curvatureStrength(turn) * 0.55.
Where curveAt gives ±0.0015; scale by 900 → ±1.35. Then drift term speedFactor*1.35*0.3? Hmm.

Let me define cornerPull(p) = clamp(curveAt(p)*1600, -1.6, 1.6) — at curveAt 0.0015 → 2.4 clamped 1.6. Then lateralResponse = steer*... - cornerPull*speedFactor*0.22. With speedFactor 1.5, corner pull 1.6 → -0.53, comparable to steering max 0.54. So on a strong corner, you must steer fully. Feels right, and lateral will saturate toward edges if you don't steer.

But there's an issue: curveAt also affects the visual track. It should be consistent — corners where you need to steer are where track bends. The sign: track bends right visually (center x increases) when dx accumulates positive. To follow the track center... actually the car camera is fixed; the track shifts. The car's lateral is relative to center. If track shifts right, the car must also move right to stay centered → lateral should increase? Visually, when the track bends right, the center at the car moves right, so player steers right (d) increasing lateral. Centrifugal pushes left, so yes: corner pull = -curve*scale? Wait if track bends right, the "outside" is left, so car is pushed left. d increases lateral right. So cornerTerm should be negative when curve positive: -curve*scale. So lateralResponse = steer*... - curve*scale*speedFactor. Hmm but that makes steering to follow the corner harder — correct.

Hmm, but is the visual bend direction correct relative to the *track*? The track center ahead bends right; player must steer right. Yes.

However, curveAt near start: at p=0, sin(0.35) positive etc. Fine.

Off track: |lateral| > 0.9 → grass, speed drops and grip loss. Add also gravel/grass visual at edges? Existing red-white kerbs and grass everywhere.

Corner cutting: if off-track, add "TRACK LIMITS" warning and small time penalty? Keep simple: reduced grip and speed loss.

Lap timing:
- car.lapStart time; lapTimes array; best lap; when progress wraps, compute lap time, show "LAP 2 — 1:32.345", update HUD lap delta.
- Add HUD display: LAST lap / BEST lap. Maybe repurpose the timer area? Add under timer small line: "LAST 1:24.312 · BEST 1:23.998" maybe in telemetry foot. Let me add a new HUD element in the bottom-left or top center under timer.

Start lights sequence:
- On RACE START click: hide start card, show 5 lights overlay at top center; each light red for 0.9 s, after 5th, hold 0.4-1.2 s random, lights out → race starts, timer starts, control unlocked. Before lights out, throttle/brake allowed? In F1, yes engine revs. Keep car stationary until lights out. Disable progress until started.

Implementation: state `phase` = 'menu' | 'lights' | 'racing' | 'finished'. `started` true only at lights out. Use raceTime for timer. Handle countdown with raceClock.

Results screen:
- On finish: show results card with position (final computed), total time, best lap, lap list, and "RACE AGAIN" button. Also allow P pause. Keep startCard styling reuse with results card new element.

Restart: reset everything.

Visual polish:
- Add start gantry with 5 light pairs above track at distance? Draw in world at start/finish? Since POV shows track ahead, the start line is behind at start. Could draw a gantry ahead at distance ~150 m from car at race start? Complex. Use overlay F1 lights in the center of the screen (like a 3D gantry): draw 5 red circles in a horizontal strip with bloom, over a dark bar. Place at upper middle (y = H*0.30). That reads well.
- Add grandstands alongside track with crowd dots, big "MONZA" signage, bridges? Some background buildings.
- Add gravel trap patches on the outside of corners (visual approximations relative to track segments).
- Add skid marks / darker asphalt patches.
- Add car detail: halo, wing endplates, exhaust glow, rear light, tyre lettering, more shading. Current car is fine but a bit flat. Add shadow and suspension arms, more contrast, carbon fiber pattern.
- Add motion blur radial at edges when fast; speed lines exist.
- Add subtle camera shake at high speed and curbs.
- Add rain? No.

Also opponents: they move at constant speeds 49-52 m/s (~180 km/h) which is way slower than the player will go (~300 km/h), so you'd lap them quickly — position becomes P1 fast. Improve: opponents should have speed ~ 70-80 m/s average with variation, and maybe be beatable. Player top speed 330; average maybe 240. Set opponent average 78 m/s (281 km/h) varying 74-80. Then player P8 with 7 cars ahead each 9 m apart is weird; they start 60 m ahead? Actually opponents progress (7-i)*9 = 63..9 m ahead of player. Player starts last P8 with -? Their progress relative to player. Actually player totalProgress = 0, opponents 9..63 m ahead. Fine.

Race pace: 3 laps of 5.793 km = 17.4 km. At avg 70 m/s → 248 s (~4 min). That's long for a demo but okay. Maybe 2 laps? User wants race mode; 3 laps fine but a 4-minute race is a lot. Monza lap at F1 pace is 1:21 (71 m/s). Opponents at 78 m/s (280 km/h avg) impossible — avg speed can't exceed ~72 m/s on Monza. Since our "track" is not geometrically accurate (no real corners slowing), it's arcade. Set opponents ~73-77 m/s.

Player speed limit ~95 m/s; average maybe 80 → lap 72 s. So the race ~3.7 min. Fine. Opponent avg 72-74 → player can win with good driving.

Add rubber banding? No.

Also opponent cars should slow in corners? Not necessary.

HUD lap delta: compute gap to car ahead based on progress difference / speed → show +0.000? Could show interval "+0.8". Let's add "GAP" element? Might be extra. Keep position, lap, timer, speed, gear as is. Add last/best lap line.

Let me also add tyre temperature and brake temp? Already temp internal not displayed. Show tyre temps? Could show "TYRE GRIP %" and 4 tyre indicators. Fine.

Mobile controls: currently display none by default? CSS probably hides. Keep.

Let me check CSS fully to know the structures.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

The engine keeps accelerating to top speed and the corners don't force slowdown because cornerPush is countered by steering without much speed loss. The player can hold full throttle the whole lap and steer; grip loss doesn't reduce speed. So the game has no need to brake. That's a simulation depth problem.

The user wanted grip loss and manual gears. The cornering push is a visual lateral force, but speed doesn't decrease in corners except off-track. We need to make cornering scrub speed and/or limit speed by grip. Add:
- Lateral acceleration demand increases tyre slip; slip should reduce speed (scrub) and increase wear.
- Cornering drag: `car.speed -= abs(latAccel)*k*dt` or a cornering resistance proportional to |latVel| and |steer|.
- If slip > 0, speed loses more.
- Steering at high speed beyond grip causes understeer: cornerPush overcomes, car goes off track; but autopilot keeps it centered at full speed. The only way to enforce braking is to make high-speed steering unable to follow the corner (it already can).

Better: make the corner push proportional to speed^2, and if the required lateral force exceeds grip, the car slides wide (lateral drift). Currently cornerPush = -bend * min(1.45, (v/55)^1.5) * .62. At high speed it caps at 1.45, but the steering authority 3.35 can easily counter. So the car can hold any corner at full speed. Real cars can't: max lateral acceleration is grip*v²/R.

We can model a speed limit for corners: the road's curvature is `bend`, and the corner radius R = 1/|bend| (units?). The generated road dx integration uses bend as curvature per meter? The visual bend is `bend` in 1/m; R ≈ 1/|bend| = 740m for .00135. At 93 m/s, lateral accel = v²/R = 8649/740 = 11.7 m/s² (1.2g) — feasible with F1 grip (4g) but the visual road curvature is not physically tied. So the car could take it flat, and the grip would still be enough. To force braking, we need much tighter corners or higher speeds. The visual bend at .00135 is gentle (Monza's Parabolica radius ~200m? Actually Parabolica R≈300m; Lesmo ~100m). Our track is 5.8km with smooth curves, so it's like a high-speed oval.

The lap time 61.8s vs real Monza 1:21 (race pace). Our track is too fast because the corners are too gentle and the car too fast. To get realistic lap times ~80s with 5.8km, the average speed must be 72 m/s (260 km/h). Real Monza average ~250 km/h. So we need corners that force slowdown to ~200-250 km/h and straights up to 330.
